claims.text: A compositionally graded HEA coating on Cu will improve coating adhesion.
The proposed coating begins with a Cu-rich transitional interlayer and shifts gradually to an HEA top layer.
HEAs can provide high wear resistance when used as coatings.
An HEA containing refractory elements such as Mo, Ta, W, and V with minor Cu is a suitable high-wear-resistant top layer.
The substrate is a Cu matrix with a standard surface finish typical of components requiring wear protection.
Magnetron sputtering with controlled substrate temperature can be used to deposit the proposed graded HEA film.
A graded interface progressively reduces chemical mismatch between the Cu substrate and the HEA coating.
A graded interface progressively reduces thermal-expansion mismatch between the Cu substrate and the HEA coating.
A Cu-rich interlayer increases interdiffusion at the Cu–HEA interface.
Increased interdiffusion from the Cu-rich interlayer enhances metallurgical bonding.
The Cu-rich interlayer minimizes interfacial stress arising from thermal-expansion differences.
Reduced interfacial stress and enhanced metallurgical bonding improve coating adhesion.
The wear-resistant HEA top layer provides durability during service.
The graded coating will produce significantly greater adhesion strength than direct deposition of the HEA coating.
The graded coating will produce a lower wear rate than direct deposition of the HEA coating.
Directly deposited wear-resistant HEA coatings on Cu typically have poor adhesion.
The poor adhesion of directly deposited HEA coatings on Cu is caused by chemical and thermal-expansion mismatches.
Performance depends on the thickness of the graded layer and the specific HEA composition.
The proposed benefit is expected under optimized magnetron-sputtering conditions.
HEA coatings on lower-cost substrates can be an economically viable alternative to bulk HEAs for harsh-environment applications.
